title: OpenAI's Altman says AI benefits warrant accepting some risks
key_facts: Altman spoke to Politico in an interview for the debut edition of Decoded, due Monday 5 Oct 2026.
He said OpenAI and Anthropic have 'a lot of daylight' between their policy positions.
He said 'the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having agency'.
He rejected regulatory-capture concerns and called concentrating powerful AI in one lab an 'unacceptable trade-off'.
He does not think society should accept 'really catastrophic risks', including a 'serious loss of control to AI'.
He declined to promise AI would eliminate hacking, fraud or other abuse.
On Saturday he posted on X that he was 'very uncomfortable' with giving AI 'religious force'.
quote_evidence: We believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having agency.
Altman said he does not believe society should accept 'really catastrophic risks'.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows a public split between OpenAI and Anthropic over how much AI risk to accept.
event_date: 4 Oct 2026 (interview published ahead of Monday 5 Oct)
notes: Reuters and Politico originals unreadable here; the Benzinga text is a short secondhand account.
